newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp fusion would save 250 mln DM -Thyssen chief.
newsitem.headline: Krupp fusion would save 250 mln DM -Thyssen chief.

text.p: A fusion of diversified German industrial groups Thyssen and Krupp would yield savings of 250 million marks a year, Thyssen chief executive Dieter Vogel said in a magazine interview released on Wednesday.

Vogel confirmed to Wirtschafts Woche magazine that the two companies, which are already in talks aimed at combining their flat-steel operations, would discuss a broader merger aimed at economies of scale, particularly in auto parts.

He said he believed there was a good chance the talks would successfully conclude by the end of the year, but that they may mean additional jobs cuts. The magazine made excerpts of the interview available ahead of the scheduled publication on Thursday.
"We would certainly not begin talking if there were not an underlying tenor of optimism," Vogel said. "If there isn't a plus for Thyssen on the bottom line, we won't do it."
Following a hostile takeover attempt by Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp in March, the two agreed to discuss merging their flat-steel operations.
An announcement on those talks is expected on September 3, and press speculation has mounted this week that the two would discuss a full merger, this time with Thyssen calling the shots.
"We will have a serious, rapid look at how far synergies can be activated beyond the steel sector. We will have the results this year," Vogel said.
Auto parts, plant construction, and trade will be three areas closely scrutinised for their savings potential, he said.
"Presumably it won't work without job cuts. But the goal cannot be a rationalisation cartel."

The steel cooperation reportedly accounts for 75 percent of the potential synergies. When the steel deal was first broached in March, Krupp chairman Gerhard Cromme said it would save 550 million marks a year after 2001.
